page: Amazon Web Services m8azn.3xlarge is a general purpose instance powered by AMD EPYC 9R05 processors operating at up to 5.0 GHz. Built on the Nitro hypervisor, the instance delivers 12 physical cores and 12 dedicated vCPUs with 1 thread per core. It is configured with 48.0 GB of high-speed DDR5 memory operating at 6 GHz, maintaining a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio of 4.0 GB per core. Network bandwidth baseline is provisioned at 25 Gbps. The instance does not include dedicated hardware accelerators (zero GPUs) or local instance storage, requiring remote Elastic Block Store (EBS) volumes for persistent storage operations.

Benchmark results highlight exceptional single-core capabilities, with the stress-ng single-core test score of 4211.18 and Geekbench single-core score of 3106.0 ranking in the top 10% tier. Instruction sets such as AVX-512, VNNI, and cryptographic extensions contribute to strong performance in data manipulation, evidenced by top-tier single-threaded gzip compression at 46.01 GB/sec and image processing scores. Memory bandwidth performance for uncached 256 MB blocks reaches 206.64 GB/sec for reads and 129.19 GB/sec for writes, both falling within the top 25%. Multi-core compute yields steady mid-to-high percentile results, including a Geekbench multi-core score of 20558.0 and PassMark CPU score of 41069.06.

The absence of hyperthreading combined with a 1:1 physical-to-virtual core allocation guarantees consistent compute performance without thread contention. Small-model LLM text generation performs in the top tier at 546.59 tokens per second, while 7B parameter models sustain 38.7 tokens per second. Resource efficiency is characterized by modern high-density DDR5 memory and high core clocks, offering solid per-core throughput at standard general-purpose tier costs. The primary hardware tradeoff is reliance entirely on networked EBS storage without ephemeral local NVMe drives.

Workload fit covers latency-sensitive compute jobs, high-throughput microservices, API backends, and caching tiers. The balanced memory density and reliable single-thread compute make it suitable for web serving, database operations, and lightweight CPU-based language model inference.

Operating with a 1:1 physical core to vCPU ratio without simultaneous multithreading, it delivers top-tier single-core compute performance alongside a 25 Gbps baseline network interface. The instance features no local storage or GPUs, relying on networked EBS volumes for disk operations. Memory throughput is strong, sustaining 206.64 GB/sec on uncached reads. Benchmark evaluations reveal top-tier single-threaded compression and small-model inference metrics, accompanied by robust multi-core Geekbench scores. The instance provides predictable compute density and low execution variance, making it well matched for web serving, containerized enterprise applications, API backends, and lightweight CPU inference workloads.
